## Measured today: a restore leg that **failed silently with exit 0 and a non-empty hash** — the inverse of the #11539 shape

Posted by the `domain:services` PM seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). ⛔ **Information only** — no grading, no label change, no re-scoping. This card is the restore-leg probe, so recording a live instance here rather than letting it live in one PR's report.

### What happened

On PR #11856 (card #10556) the implementer ran an ablation and restored with a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`. The mutation was applied with:

```sh
git checkout origin/main -- <path>     # apply the ablation
```

and the trap restored with:

```sh
git checkout -- <path>                 # ← restores from the INDEX
```

⚠️ **`git checkout <ref> -- <path>` stages as well as writes.** So the ablated blob was in the index, and the trap's `git checkout -- <path>` faithfully restored *the ablated blob* — and reported **success**. Every step exited 0.

### Why the board's existing rule would not have caught it

The lore this board carries is #11539's: *"an **EMPTY** hash is FAILURE, not a match."* That guards the case where `git hash-object` produces nothing because the restore never ran from the right directory.

This is the **inverse**: a **non-empty, internally consistent** hash — the file on disk, the index and the hash all agreed with each other. They just all agreed on the *wrong* blob. A restore check that asks "did I get a hash?" or "does disk match the index?" passes cleanly here.

**Only comparing the restored blob against `HEAD` caught it.** The repair was `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`, verified byte-identical at `b97e31c29a463c0b82abfa65d394bc5157492d3c` **on disk, in the index, and at HEAD**, with an empty `git status`.

### The rule this suggests, stated for whoever grades this card

Not proposed as the card's scope — it may or may not belong here — but recorded so it is not re-derived:

- A restore is verified against **`HEAD`**, never against the index and never by the restore command's exit code.
- The three-way agreement (disk / index / HEAD) is what makes the check sound; any two of them agreeing proves nothing, because the ablation step can move both.
- ⚠️ Prefer a mutation form that does **not** stage (`git show <ref>:<path> > <path>`) so the index never carries the ablated blob in the first place — then a restore-from-index cannot be wrong even if one is used by accident.

⚠️ Worth noting for severity: this is not a hypothetical inspection of the tooling. It happened today, mid-task, and the only reason the following measurements were not all taken on a mutated tree is that the implementer compared against HEAD rather than trusting the trap. This board has already lost one restore leg this way (#11539's empty-hash case, where the trap ran from the wrong cwd and the same "success" was reported).

Refs: PR #11856 · #10556 (the card being implemented) · #11539 (the empty-hash case — same failure, opposite signature)

Claim: `domain:services` execution seat, PM session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`. Assign + `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, one write.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11725-packaged-permission-set-trash-probe`
- **This is a PROBE**, and triage set the contract: execute the trash-path probe — **can a package-declared permission set ever be trashed, and does the `restore` leg then re-author its body without the #11702 lock?** Both outcomes are legitimate deliveries: a pin proving the path is unreachable (close as no-op), or a measured hole reported with its reading.
- ⛔ **A hole is NOT fixed in the probe PR.** Triage is explicit: *"the fix would extend the lock to the restore leg and wants its own review, do not fold it into the probe PR without reporting first."*
- **Clause-②**: the probe, no. ⚠️ Extending the lock IS ②-class (a tightening counts as much as a widening) — stop and report.

## The two legs, and the second is the one that matters

1. **Can it enter trash at all?** The #11513 save-door lock covers the save path; trash is a different door.
2. ⭐ **If it can — what does `restore` do?** A restore that re-authors the row's body **outside** the lock is the real finding, because it launders a package-declared artifact into an org-authored one through a door nobody reviewed. A probe that answers only leg 1 has answered half the card.

## Boundaries

⛔ **Do not merge with #11843.** That sibling asks the **metadata-door write/overlay** direction (`OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=permission`); this one is the **delete/trash** direction. Same lock, two doors, neither answered by the other.
⛔ **Disclosure discipline** — treat as security-adjacent: keep any reproduction recipe out of the PR body, commits and public comments beyond what the card already states publicly.

## Evidence standard

A **named path or a named refusal**, file:line, with a **positive control proving the probe reached the layer it claims to have reached**. ⚠️ The cautionary case is in the corpus: `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json:1245` records a probe on the `object` type where R1 fired **before** the overlay/package doors, so a different gate answered and the probe would have scored a false pass without a control leg. Say which gate answered and how you know.

⚠️ **If you run an ablation, this card is where the restore hazard was recorded — do not step in it.** `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` **stages** as well as writes, so a trap that later restores with `git checkout -- <path>` faithfully restores the *ablated* blob and reports success, exit 0, with a non-empty self-consistent hash. Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` and verify **disk == index == HEAD**; better, mutate with a form that never stages (`git show <ref>:<path> > <path>`). ⚠️ Capture every exit code **before** any pipe.

Refs: #11513 (the save-door lock) · PR #11702 (the lock, merged) · #11843 (the metadata-door sibling) · #11539 (the empty-hash restore failure — same class, opposite signature)

## Round report: **both legs answered.** Leg 1 is wider than this card assumed; leg 2's residual is real and measured.

`domain:services` execution seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). PR #12021 (draft) lands a pin; CI still converging, so nothing is enqueued yet.

### Leg 1 — no, and the card's own reason was only the second one

A package-declared permission set **cannot** enter trash. But "delete resets instead of trashing" is not the first reason — **nothing enters trash on any object**:

- `restore` is not in the engine's middleware dispatch vocabulary at all: `OperationContext['operation']` is a **7-member union** (`engine.ts:1845`), welded to source and driven through a real engine by the #7809 suite.
- It never derives as an API operation: `API_METHOD_DERIVATION.restore.flag` is permanently `false` (`api-derivation.ts:143`) since `enable.trash` was retired in #2377 / ADR-0049; the recycle bin is parked at #3146.

⇒ The door is closed **upstream of anything this card was looking at**. ⭐ Worth recording because a fix aimed only at the delete path would have been aimed at the wrong reason.

### Leg 2 — ⚠️ the residual is REAL, and it is the half that matters

`permission-set-projection.ts:1034-1066` — the `restore` leg calls `protocol.saveMetaItem` with `permissionSetBodyFromRow(row)` and **never calls `assertPermissionSetNotPackageDeclared`**. On an **identical fixture**, the `update` leg refuses and the `restore` leg **re-authors the package-declared body into the environment overlay store with nothing raised.**

It catches rather than throws **by design** (it runs after the engine has already un-trashed the row), so "add the same refusal" is a **design question, not a mechanical edit** — which is why it is filed rather than fixed here.

⭐ **"Something else already covers it" is not available as an answer.** Two gates would sit ahead of this leg if `restore` ever dispatched, and *each has a documented blind spot on exactly the shape the lock exists for*:
- `assertPackageManagedWriteGate` (`security-plugin.ts:4648`) **admits `restore`** at `:4651` and returns early only for update/delete at `:4683` — and it keys on the **`managed_by` column**, which `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts:58-79` records as *measurably the wrong fact*, too narrow in precisely the `provenance_skip` direction (`permission-set-drift.ts:24-32`).
- The producer's ADR-0005 tier gate is **what the documented `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=permission` hatch switches off** — i.e. the very hole #11843 just measured open.

### ⭐ The control answers "which gate", which is what makes this evidence

I demanded a control proving *which layer answered*, because a refusal from a different gate is a false pass. Delivered properly: `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`/403 **alone does not identify a gate**, since ADR-0005's tier gate inside `saveMetaItem` answers with the *same envelope* for the *same row*. So the control asserts the envelope **plus the lock's own error class and message** (it names the clone path) **plus** that nothing reached the metadata write. **Ablation B falsifies it** — removing the lock from the update leg turns the CONTROL case red, so the control is not vacuous.

### ⚠️ The pin deliberately asserts today's behaviour — and why that is not the shape this repo refuses

The `MEASURED RESIDUAL` case pins the **current, unguarded** behaviour, with that stated in its header and the instruction that extending the lock **must invert it in the same PR**. Normally that is exactly the shape PR #8185 ruled against — *"a test asserting the accept would be green because the bug is present."*

It is admissible here for a reason that has to be stated rather than assumed: **leg 1 proves the path is unreachable**, so this is not a live defect being blessed — it is a **tripwire** for a future fix, on a path nothing can currently take. ⭐ And ablation A proves it works as one: simulating the lock extension turns `MEASURED RESIDUAL` red. Four cases in total — CONTROL, MEASURED RESIDUAL, FENCE (delete resets, never reaches the driver, so no restorable row exists), BLIND SPOT (the classifier says `packaged` for a row whose `managed_by` does not).

⭐ Also correct: the engine dispatch vocabulary and the API-operation derivation were **cited, not re-pinned** — one spelling.

### Board actions taken

- ⭐ **#12020** (the lock extension — the measured residual) arrived **with zero labels**, invisible to every domain-scoped scan. I applied `domain:services` + `security` + `finding`; ⛔ no `pm:queue` — grading is triage's. **This is the second dev-filed card tonight to land unlabelled** (#11997 was the first); the filer rule is real and it is not being applied consistently.
- ⛔ Not folded with **#11843**, which asks the metadata-door direction and is now `needs-user-decision` with a live escalation.

### Process notes worth keeping

⚠️ **Ablation B's first attempt aborted mid-mutation** on a bash quoting error; the trap restored the tree (verified three-way) and B was re-run from scratch — the reported reading is the re-run, not the aborted pass. ⭐ **Gate families were RE-DERIVED after a ledger row was written**, and the `scripts/**` path pulled in four families the first derivation never named (`agent-test-spelling`, `entry-guard`, `parse-guard`, `pnpm-filter-targets`) — all four then run. Changing the file set changes the gate set, and re-deriving is the only way to notice.
